faqs.question: What is the LZC Photoreactor used for?
faqs.answer: It's a closed-chamber benchtop irradiation system built for photochemistry, photobiology, organic synthesis, materials science, and teaching applications requiring uniform light exposure across multiple samples.

faqs.question: How do I change the wavelength on my LZC Photoreactor?
faqs.answer: Lamps pull out and swap in without tools, so switching between UVA, UVC, or another wavelength in the LZC-Series range takes seconds, not a system rebuild.

faqs.question: What's the difference between the four LZC packages?
faqs.answer: They differ mainly in lamp geometry: LZC-4V combines top and side illumination, LZC-1 runs top lamps only, LZC-ORG runs side lamps only, and LZC-4X offers a fourth confirmed configuration.

faqs.question: Can I use lamps from a Rayonet reactor in my LZC Photoreactor?
faqs.answer: Many Rayonet-compatible lamps work with LZC hardware, since both platforms share compatibility across much of the same lamp range.

faqs.question: What comes standard with the LZC-4V package?
faqs.answer: Six top lamps and eight side lamps, two complete lamp sets (14 UVA at 367nm and 14 UVC at 254nm), a carousel and turntable, magnetic stirrer, timer, gas inlet, hour meter, safety interlock, UVA power meter, exhaust kit, and safety glasses.

faqs.question: How does the carousel and turntable work?
faqs.answer: Both run off the same integrated motor drive, with the carousel handling test tubes and the turntable handling solid samples.

faqs.question: What safety features are standard across all packages?
faqs.answer: A safety interlock, integrated timer, hour meter, bulkhead gas connector, safe exhaust system, and safety glasses ship with every LZC package.

faqs.question: What power supply does the LZC Photoreactor need?
faqs.answer: It runs on 120/240V, suited to benchtop use without a separate power converter.

sections.description: LZC Photoreactor product information: chamber design, package options, and lamp compatibility.
sections.subheading: Why lamp flexibility defines this platform
body: Most photoreactors lock you into one wavelength setup until you're ready to buy a new unit. LZC lamps pull out and swap in without a single tool, opening the same chamber to the complete LZC-Series UV and visible lamp range, and much of the Rayonet range too.

A 12 x 12 x 8.5 inch air-cooled chamber keeps every sample under uniform light, whether the package puts lamps overhead, along the sides, or both. The LZC-4V package, the most popular configuration, pairs six top lamps with eight side lamps and ships with two complete lamp sets, 14 UVA at 367nm and 14 UVC at 254nm, so switching wavelength families is a lamp change, not a new purchase.

Every package runs the same safety backbone: an interlock, integrated timer, hour meter, bulkhead gas connector, safety glasses, and a safe exhaust system, on 120/240V power for straightforward benchtop use anywhere.

sections.title: Chamber Design and Package Configurations
sections.description: Getting uniform light across multiple samples starts with chamber geometry, and LZC solves it with a spacious, air-cooled 12 x 12 x 8.5 inch chamber that keeps every sample under consistent irradiation rather than a hot spot at the center. Where the four packages differ is lamp placement. LZC-4V combines top and side illumination for full-coverage work and doubles as a two-wavelength platform with its included UVA and UVC lamp sets. LZC-1 concentrates eight lamps overhead for applications that call for top-down exposure specifically, and LZC-ORG runs ten side lamps for a different geometry entirely. LZC-4X offers a fourth configuration, and a related LZC-ICH2 unit shows up in the broader product lineup for specialized needs.

sections.title: Tool-Free Lamp Swapping and Safety Features
sections.description: A reactor that locks you into one wavelength stops being useful the moment your research changes direction. LZC lamps pull and swap without tools, so a new experiment with a different wavelength requirement doesn't mean a new reactor purchase.
body: That flexibility extends beyond Luzchem's own lamp range. The same hardware accepts the complete LZC-Series UV and visible fluorescent and LED lamp lineup, and much of that range is also compatible with many Rayonet reactors, useful if your lab already has lamps on hand from elsewhere. Every package backs that flexibility with the same safety foundation: an interlock that stops irradiation when the chamber opens, an integrated timer and hour meter for tracking exposure and lamp life, and a safe exhaust system for managing fumes during longer runs.
